title: Automatic exit remains an obligation across application and leadership changes
support: API promise and tests; alternate schedules derived from API
scope: An applied or restored joint AutoLeave configuration; a healthy stable leader remains a voter.
predicate: Track joint episode e and its establishing entry/snapshot index j, actual configuration installation, and inherited-tail barrier b recorded at current leader election (or j when this leader enters e). These are history facts, not aliases of mutable P.

Eligible(e) means current installed configuration is e with O nonempty and AutoLeave, local node is leader in I union O, A>=max(j,b), and no retained exit for e exists and no earlier retained configuration with index>A remains. A retained exit still discharges the proposal obligation when A passed its index but its actual application is deferred.

On the normal path, Advance(B) acknowledging the entering entry after ApplyConfChange installed it must append one semantic leave in the same call when no exit is already retained. It must not fail/panic because of quota. New behavior uses empty Data and zero payload cost.

More generally, with a stable eligible leader, fair local ticks/Ready service, and eventual completion of deferred application, Eligible(e) leads to an exit proposal even when A already reached j before AutoLeave was installed or before leadership began. With available joint quorums, eventual message delivery, persistence, and ordered application, that exit is eventually applied and O becomes empty and AutoLeave=false. No new client proposal is assumed.

Automatic exit generation requires an installed joint AutoLeave configuration and a leader. Explicit/manual joint configurations are not auto-left. HardState.Commit beyond j alone is not acknowledgement of applying j.

evidence.basis: Implicit transitions/AutoLeave promise automatic exit when safe; explicit transitions wait for the application.
Advance can precede completion of application; ApplyConfChange is a separate action.
Advance initiates auto-exit; new strict cursor crossing interacts with inherited barrier.
Processing entering change creates next-Ready exit, then joint replication applies it.
Implicit exit versus explicit context-bearing manual exit.

history: exit application completion, distinct from A crossing its index

old_new_interaction: Old level-triggered attempts could be quota-blocked or duplicated. New zero-cost behavior is permitted and required on the normal path; its edge-triggered guard cannot narrow the API promise. Leadership/deferred-application examples are static risks, not executed counterexamples.
limits: No unconditional progress under permanent partition, absent quorum, stopped callers, endless leadership changes, or storage unavailability.
